title: jadi — so
pattern: A, jadi B · Jadi, … · A, makanya B
explanation: jadi gives the result: first what happened, then jadi and what followed from it: Hujan, jadi kami di rumah. — It was raining, so we stayed in. It's karena the other way round: Kami di rumah karena hujan says the same thing. Like English so, Jadi at the start of a sentence also sums up or gets back to the point: Jadi, semuanya berapa? makanya means that's why, often when something finally makes sense: Oh, makanya kamu capek! — Oh, that's why you're tired!
natural: Everyday and neutral, spoken or written. Jadi, … to sum up is everywhere: in shops, at work and in stories.
stiff: Formal writing uses sehingga or oleh karena itu, which sound like an essay in a chat. makanya can also scold (see, that's why!), so take care with it to someone older. And jadi has other meanings too: to become (jadi guru) and to go ahead as planned (Besok jadi?).

examples.english: The shop was closed, so we went home.

gap.why: Going home is the result of the shop being closed: jadi, so.

examples.indonesian: Saya tidak bisa makan pedas, jadi sambalnya sedikit saja.
examples.english: I can't eat spicy food, so just a little chilli sauce, please.

gap.why: First the situation, then what follows from it: jadi.

examples.english: So, how much is that altogether?

gap.why: Jadi at the start sums up and moves things on: so, all told.

examples.english: I didn't get enough sleep, that's why I've got a headache.

gap.note: jadi works too; makanya points at the cause a little harder: that's why.
gap.why: makanya means that's why, with the cause before it.
